what: At Kumbh and Adh-Kumbh the corporate bodies (akharas) of ascetic sects attend in state and march in procession on Sankrant, Amawas, Basant Panchmi; 1906 Kumbh three million present
quote: the corporate bodies of the various sects of religious ascetics attend the fair in state

what: Quarrel among Bairagi akharas (Nirbanis vs Nirmohis and Digambaris) in 1906 needed a squadron of cavalry
quote: a danger of conflict among the Bairagis, between the Nirbanis on one side and the Nirmohis and Digambaris on the other

what: Nirbanis, first in precedence in the procession, are Naga Goshains, followers of Siva; used to go naked
quote: First come the Nirbanis, who) sre/Naga Goshains, followers of Siva

what: Niranjanis, associated with Junas, are Saivites who go naked, belong chiefly to Daraganj, wealthy and carry on extensive banking
quote: The Niranjanis, associated in the processions with a similar fraternity called Junas, are also Saivites and go naked

what: Niranjani akhara equally wealthy, extensive banking business
quote: They are equally wealthy and carry on an extensive banking business

what: Large houses of Niranjani and Nirmali akharas; Daraganj residence of numerous Faqirs
quote: there are large houses belonging to the Niranjani and Nirmali akharas

what: Akharas at Daraganj among large bankers: Mahant Partabgir Goshain and the Panchayati Akhara of the Mahanirbani Goshains (also Gokul Das Batragi)
quote: notably those of Gokul Das Batragi, Mahant Partabgir Goshain and the Panchayati Akhara of the Mahanirbani Goshains

what: Bairagis all Vaishnavites, wandering mendicants, three divisions Nirbanis, Nirmohis, Digambaris, make no outward display in the procession
quote: The Bairagis are all Vaishnavites and are wandering mendicants without any fixed residence

what: Chhota Panchayati Akhara, Udasis of the Punjab, large monastery in Mutiganj; originally Sikhs, now Hindus; Bara Panchayati Akhara in Kydganj, wealthy bankers
quote: Then comes the Chhota Panchayati Akhara, a body of Udasis of the Punjab, who have a large monastery in Mutiganj

what: Bara Panchayati Akhara, offshoot, large house, very wealthy and makes much money by banking; Nanakshahis of Bandhua Hasanpur (Sultanpur) join the fair
quote: An offshoot of this body is the Bara Panchayati Akhara in Kydganj

what: Nirmalis, still Sikhs in principle, live in the Pili Kothi in Kydganj, considerable bankers; Bindrabani Nanakshahis join their procession
quote: Lastly come the Nirmalis, who are still Sikhs in principle

what: Large numbers of Sannyasis also frequent the fair and have a separate encampment
quote: large numbers of Sannyasis frequent the fair and have a separate encampment

what: Ramanujis of Daraganj among the richest and largest communities; Ramanandis of the dharmsala of Baba Hari Das in Kydganj; both Tyagis living on alms
quote: The Ramanujis of Daraganj are one of the richest and largest communities in Allahabad

what: Mahant Dharam Das of Kydganj owns two villages and 38 mahals, revenue Rs 6,033; order not stated
quote: Mahant Dharam Das of Kydganj owris two villages and 38 mahals in Phulpur assessed at Rs. 6,033

what: Indargir Goshain came to Allahabad on pilgrimage with 5,000 naked Sannyasis and sided with Oudh against Ahmad Khan in the siege (1750s)

what: Goshains hold 1.2 per cent of the land of the district

what: Small remainder of land owned by Goshains and Ahirs

what: Goshains hold 2.16 per cent of the area
